newsitem.title: SPAIN: RALLING-THIRY AND LIATTI LEAD CATALONIA RALLY.
newsitem.headline: RALLING-THIRY AND LIATTI LEAD CATALONIA RALLY.

text.p: Belgian Ford driver Bruno Thiry and Italy's Piero Liatti in a Subaru were joint leaders of the Catalonia Rally at the end of the third stage of the 1.368-km race on Monday.

Thiry -- who could be dropped by his team at the end of the season -- remains Ford's only hope in the final round of the World Rally Championship after double world champion Carlos Sainz rolled his Ford on the second stage.
Sainz, competing in front of his home crowd, slid out on a wet corner on an otherwise dry asphalt road.
Thiry said he would have crashed on the same corner if he had not been warned by Sainz's co-driver, Luis Moya, but lost his hold on the lead briefly by spinning at the stage finish.
"I'm surprised -- positively surprised. The car is fantastic," Thiry said.
Thiry and Liatti were seven seconds clear of Subaru team leader Colin McRae of Britain with Belgium's Freddie Loix in a Toyota a further four seconds back.
New world champion Tommi Makinen in a Mitsubishi slid off the road and clipped a wall on the same corner which claimed Sainz and was 21 seconds behind the joint leaders.
